documents.title: San Antonio will consider regulating data centers. It is unclear if that involves a moratorium.
documents.text: Council heard proposed zoning changes at a special meeting; no moratorium vote. Councilman Jalen McKee-Rodriguez (D2): "Data centers are one of the largest, fastest-growing threats to our communities," Councilman Ric Galvan (D6): "I’d prefer that we do as much as possible as quickly as possible," Resident/advocate Deedee Belmares (Public Citizen): "My biggest concern is the 500-foot setback," Councilwoman Misty Spears (D9): "Data center development greatly supports the commercial construction industry," Development Services director Amin Tohmaz said a moratorium is "a temporary measure," not a permanent stop.

documents.title: Breaking down the options for data center rules in San Antonio
documents.text: Stephanie Reyes, president of the Real Estate Council of San Antonio, said: "Anytime we want to attract investment, there has to be consistency and predictability." Deedee Belmares, a Public Citizen clean energy advocate, said: "It's so important for you all to recommend to City Council this specific use authorization" Mayor Gina Ortiz Jones said: "We understand the importance of this computing power for our national security and our economic security," Jones also said: "We should not also be attractive as, frankly, being a cheap date."

documents.title: San Antonio Data Center Regulations Pass in 9-2 City Council Vote
documents.text: Council voted 9-2 to limit new data centers to heavy commercial and industrial zoning districts and to require a Specific Use Authorization for each. Councilman Ric Galvan (District 6): "The residents of San Antonio deserve to have a say in where and how data centers are built in our city," "All new data centers within city limits should require a vote by City Council." "This is the only way to ensure that our community has a meaningful voice in data center development in San Antonio."
